description: Runs the guided consult "Fix my prime cost" one step at a time from the answers so far, as RestaurantDoctorAI's AI restaurant expert does on restaurantdoctorai.com: the 6 set questions (type of restaurant, a week or a month, net sales, food and drink invoices, wages, payroll taxes and benefits), a check on any figure that looks like a slip, the free prime cost calculator's result, then up to 5 more questions on the half that comes first, ending in one finding: the biggest problem at these figures, the step-by-step fix to start with, its sources and at most two other things worth a look. Fixed rules and the calculators produce every figure and sentence, with no AI in between. Nothing is kept between calls: the answers so far come in on every call, each one optional, and the reply is the first step still open, with the fields and set answers that answer it. Any number of answers can come in one call. A figure that isn't sent is never counted as 0. A dish is only its price, plate cost and number sold, with no name. A guide, not a promise of results, and not legal, tax or financial advice. The figures aren't stored; only an anonymous daily count of calculator runs is kept.

anyOf.description: True for the other half's questions as well, when it's over its range too. They come after the finding and aren't part of it.
Optional: stock at cost at the end of the period, counted on the same items the invoices cover. Used only with openingStock.
The checks the owner says are right, by the id each check step gives.
Whether the owner knows what their best sellers cost to plate.
Up to 3 best sellers, drinks included, for the same dates as the other figures. All 3 can come in one call, and a call's list is the whole list.

plateCost.description: What one costs to plate, in the same currency.

price.description: Its menu price, in the same currency as the other figures.

sold.description: How many sold, for the same dates as the other figures.

anyOf.description: True when the list of dishes is finished at fewer than 3, or empty.
Which figures are the owner's own rough estimate: each reads "(your estimate)" where the figures are shown.
Which half comes first when food and drink and labor tie: the answer to the tie step.

The type of restaurant, which sets the targets: prime cost, and the ranges for food and drink and for labor: quick_service = Quick service (Counter or kiosk, fast turnover); fast_casual = Fast casual (Order at the counter, served at the table); full_service = Full service / casual dining (Servers, moderate check); fine_dining = Fine dining (Chef-driven, higher check); bar_lounge = Bar, taproom or lounge (Drinks are about half of sales or more); cafe = Café or coffee shop (Drinks lead, with pastries and light food).
How much of the wages figure was hourly pay. The rest counts as salaries.
The hours hourly staff worked, overtime included, from the time clock.
Optional: stock at cost at the start of the period. Used only with closingStock: food and drink then becomes what was used, opening + purchases - closing.
How many of those hours were overtime.

Optional: when the owner works in the restaurant without a salary, what they'd pay someone to do their hours, plus the payroll taxes on it. It's a second figure; the main one stays as the books have it.
Optional: the employer's payroll taxes and benefits for the period, such as health insurance or a pension, when the wages figure leaves them out.
True when the wages figure already has payroll taxes and benefits in it. A payrollCosts figure then isn't counted.
Whether every figure covers one week or one month, the same dates for all of them. Sets how a year is worked out (52 weeks or 12 months).
Food and drink supplier invoices for the same dates, added up by delivery date, minus credits. No packaging. Needed for a result; if missing, the reply asks for it.
True once the result step has been seen. The questions on why come after it, and the finding doesn't repeat the result's lines.

Net sales for the period, in the owner's own currency like every figure here, from the POS sales summary: after discounts and comps, before tax and tips, with any service charge paid out to staff added back. Needed for a result, and more than 0; if missing, the reply asks for it.
The steps the owner passed on: payrollCosts, stock, hourlyWages, hours, overtimeHours and owner. The others stay open.
False when the owner doesn't work in the restaurant without a salary.

Every wage and salary for the same dates, from payroll, managers included (a salary counts as a 52nd of a year for a week, a 12th for a month). No tips, but a service charge paid to staff stays in. Needed for a result; if missing, the reply asks for it.
